brand: Daehan New Pharm Co., Ltd. (South Korea)
description: Luthione is a reduced (L-)glutathione injectable supplied as a sterile lyophilised powder for reconstitution, available in 600 mg and 1200 mg per-vial strengths. It is used in clinician-administered IV/IM protocols for antioxidant support, skin brightening and general wellness. Each pack typically contains 10 vials for in-clinic course-based treatment.
howItWorks: Glutathione is a cysteine-glycine-glutamate tripeptide that acts as a major intracellular antioxidant, neutralising reactive oxygen species and supporting hepatic detoxification (phase II conjugation) pathways. Its reported skin-brightening effect is attributed to inhibition of tyrosinase and a shift of melanogenesis from darker eumelanin toward lighter pheomelanin, reducing melanin deposition. Delivered parenterally to bypass gastrointestinal breakdown of oral glutathione.
composition: Reduced glutathione (L-glutathione) 600 mg or 1200 mg per vial; white lyophilised powder reconstituted before administration.
usageNotes: Prescription-only injectable to be reconstituted and administered by trained medical staff via slow IV push, IV drip or IM injection; not for self-administration. Screen for G6PD deficiency before high-dose glutathione therapy owing to haemolysis risk, and take a full history including asthma, pregnancy/lactation and prior reactions. Reconstitute immediately before use, inspect for particulates, and observe the patient for hypersensitivity; typical aesthetic courses run once daily/weekly over roughly 10 sessions per clinician judgement.

description: Cindella is a thioctic acid (alpha-lipoic acid) injectable antioxidant supplied as ampoules of 25 mg in 5 mL, packaged 10 ampoules per box. It is widely used as the antioxidant component of clinician-administered IV brightening and skin-revitalisation programs, often paired with glutathione and vitamin C. Administration is by a qualified medical professional.
howItWorks: Thioctic acid (alpha-lipoic acid) is a unique antioxidant that is both lipid- and water-soluble, allowing it to act in cell membranes and cytosol where vitamins C and E cannot independently reach. It scavenges free radicals and helps regenerate other antioxidants including vitamin C, vitamin E and glutathione, reinforcing the cellular antioxidant network that underlies brighter, more even-looking skin. This complementary action is why it is commonly co-administered with glutathione and vitamin C.
composition: Thioctic acid (alpha-lipoic acid) 25 mg per 5 mL ampoule; 10 ampoules per box.
usageNotes: Prescription injectable administered by a certified medical professional, typically by slow intravenous infusion (often diluted per protocol) and shielded from light due to photosensitivity of the active. Take a full history including diabetes/hypoglycaemia risk (ALA may lower blood glucose), thiamine status, pregnancy/lactation and prior reactions; monitor during infusion for hypersensitivity. When combined with high-dose glutathione or vitamin C, screen for G6PD deficiency as part of the antioxidant-cocktail workup.

description: Vita-D 200,000 IU is a Korean cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) injectable containing 5 mg (200,000 IU) per ampoule, used for the prevention and treatment of vitamin D deficiency in adults. It is administered by intramuscular injection under medical supervision and is typically supplied in boxes of 5 or 10 ampoules. The specific manufacturer is not independently confirmed in available trade listings.
howItWorks: Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) is converted in the liver to 25-hydroxyvitamin D and then in the kidney to the active hormone calcitriol, which regulates intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption and bone mineralisation. A single high-dose intramuscular depot raises and sustains serum 25(OH)D levels, correcting deficiency where oral repletion is impractical or adherence is poor. It addresses nutrient status rather than acting as a skin-brightening agent.
composition: Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) 5 mg = 200,000 IU per ampoule (1 mL).
usageNotes: Prescription injectable administered intramuscularly by a clinician; high-dose vitamin D should be dosed on the basis of baseline serum 25(OH)D and clinical need to avoid hypervitaminosis D and hypercalcaemia. Take a history for hypercalcaemia, hypercalciuria, nephrolithiasis, sarcoidosis/granulomatous disease and renal impairment, and avoid stacking with other high-dose vitamin D sources. Monitor calcium and 25(OH)D on repeat dosing and observe for injection-site reactions.
